name.description: The extension's name; must equal its folder's.

namespace.description:
The namespace its commands' ids are under
(`<namespace>.<area>.<verb>`); defaults to the name with `-` → `_`.
`oxplow` is reserved for the extensions that ship with oxplow.

engine.description: The oxplow version range it targets, `>=MAJOR.MINOR[.PATCH]`.

version.description:
Its own version, `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` (semver; a `-pre` suffix is
fine). Recorded on every contribution it makes.

intent.description:
Why it exists: its purpose, the ref that created it, and examples.
Required.

purpose.description: The question it answers, or the job it does.

origin.description: The thread or effort ref that created it (`oxplow:oxplow/effort?id=eff42`), when known.

prompts.description:
Questions it helps answer, offered to the person with an Ask
button (the catalog; pages for a ref of `about`'s kind).

exports.description: Explicit versioned contracts offered to other extensions.

imports.description: Consumer-local bindings to canonical public contributions.

import_guards.description: Contributions to withhold when one of these bindings is unavailable.

configuration.description:
Versioned non-secret settings schema and partial defaults. Read raw so
declaration errors never format configuration values into diagnostics.

requires.description:
The other extensions it needs on (`.context/extensions.md`
"Requires"): deploying or turning it on refuses while one is off,
and turning one off refuses while this is on.

build.description:
A command a deploy runs in the source folder before it copies
(`.context/extensions.md` "Builds"). Read raw so a broken block is
its own error at its line.

permissions.description:
What it may reach beyond the baseline (`.context/extensions.md`
"Permissions"): checked against what it contains when it loads,
approved when it is deployed.

models.description:
SQL models: each with `models/<name>.sql`, published as
`v_<extension>_<name>`.

collectors.description:
Collectors (exec / starlark / jaq / read), writing entities or
recording facts.

commands.description:
Commands: a Starlark script composing core commands, a scope's
operation, or one of its provider's.

jobs.description: Durable host operations that an extension may schedule.

ai_profiles.description:
Named model needs: the person binds `<extension>/<id>` to a model,
else the fallback role's model serves it.

pages.description: Full pages, each showing one of its lenses.

panels.description: Left-nav panels, each showing its lenses compact.

ui.description: What it adds to the core UI: slots, decorators, replacements.

advisories.description:
Guidance queries run at a moment (`on`), whose rows reach the
agent or a person.

event_types.description: The event types it may log, under its own namespace.

implementations.description: Capability implementations: built-ins of core's it declares.

skills.description: Skills and slash commands for the coding agent.

providers.description:
External providers: programs implementing a capability, whose
operations its `commands:` declare.

effects.description: Scripts reacting to logged events by composing commands.

custom_components.description: Sandboxed web components for `viz: custom` lenses.

IntentExample.description:
One acceptance example: an input and what the extension should make
of it. Fixtures for `oxplow extension test`; data here.

IntentPrompt.description:
A question an extension helps answer. `about` is a ref kind
(`commit`, `file`, `effort`): a page for a ref of that kind suggests it.

version.description:
The contract version it was written for; absent, whatever the
producer exports binds.

ConfigurationFile.description:
A versioned declaration of non-secret settings. This is data, not consent
or a credential reference. Stored overrides and host services are separate.

migrations.description:
How a layer stored at an older `version` becomes the declared one:
steps that chain without gaps up to `version`.

ConfigMigration.description:
One step of a configuration schema migration: a pure Starlark
`transform(values) -> values` (the extension's `entry`, relative to its
folder) from stored schema version `from` to `to`.

Build.description:
What a deploy builds before it copies: `run` in the source folder, as
the person, then `output` is copied into the deployment. The hash is of
the inputs — every file but `output` and the `exclude` folders — and
`run` itself, so a build's output never changes what is deployed.

run.description:
The command, run with `/bin/sh -c` in the source folder with the
person's environment. A new or changed one is approved at deploy.

output.description:
The folder it writes (`dist`), relative to the extension: copied
into the deployment, never hashed.

Permissions.description:
What an extension may do beyond the baseline. Absent fields grant
nothing.

sql.description: Ad-hoc SQL: a script's `scope("sql.read")`, a component's own query.

commands.description:
Commands outside its own namespace it may run, as patterns:
`oxplow.work_item.*` (`*` is one segment, `**` the rest).

files.description: The project's files outside the bus.

ai.description: Calling AI models, with the person's key.

network.description: The hosts its programs may reach (`api.github.com`, `*.example.com`).

process.description:
Running programs (providers, `exec` collectors). They run with the
person's authority; oxplow doesn't confine them.

secrets.description: The secrets it may read, by name.

agent.description: Contributing to the agent's context: skills, advisories, prompts.

SqlAccess.description: `sql: read`: ad-hoc read-only SQL over the `v_*` models.

FilesAccess.description:
`files: read | write`: the project's files outside the bus. `write`
includes `read`.

ModelDecl.description: One model as its owner declares it (an entry of `models.yaml`).

columns.description: The contract: the view's columns, in order.

key.description:
The columns whose values name one row: declared columns,
part of the contract. A key implies its test (never null, never
repeated), and a materialized model's table takes it as its
primary key.

deprecated.description:
Earlier versions kept published beside this one after a breaking
change, each as `<view>_v<version>` until its date.

materialize.description:
How it is computed: absent, on read (a view); `on_change`, stored
and recomputed when one of its inputs changes; `{ every: 1h }`,
stored and recomputed on that clock.

type.description:
The declared type SQLite reports for the view's column
(`PRAGMA table_info`); empty for a computed column.

TestDecl.description:
One declared test, written as a one-key map: `{ not_null: id }`,
`{ unique: id }`, `{ accepted_values: { column, values } }`,
`{ relationships: { column, to, field } }` or `{ sql: "SELECT …" }` (a
query returning the failing rows).

to.description: The model the column points into.

Deprecated.description:
An earlier version kept after a breaking change: its SQL (in `file`,
beside the model's) still keeps the contract that version published,
until `until` (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

Materialize.description:
A model's freshness policy beyond the default (computed on read):
`on_change`, or `{ every: 1h }`.

anyOf.description:
Stored and recomputed, whole, on a clock — `{ every: 1h }` (the
collectors' grammar: minutes `15m` or hours `2h`) — whatever its
inputs do: for SQL that reads the time (`'now'`), whose answer
moves without a write.

Stored, and kept by appending the rows past its watermark —
`{ incremental: <column> }`, a declared INTEGER that only grows —
refilled whole when an input saw a rewrite.

oneOf.description: Stored in its table and recomputed, whole, when an input changes.

MeasureEntry.description:
One entry in the top-level `measures:` block — the **measure catalog**
authoring surface. A measure is a *type of atomic
fact* a collector may emit (`oxplow.complexity`, `acme.api_latency`, …); the
`oxplow.*` built-ins are seeded by the DB migration, so config only *adds*
global/project measures. Unlike [`MetricEntry`] there is no `use:`/`key:`
split — a measure entry is always a definition (you declare the fact type,
you don't "enable" one). Resolved across the global+project scopes by
[`resolve_measures`] and seeded into the `measure` table at boot.

key.description: The new measure's namespaced key (`<vendor>.<id>`). Required.

captureScope.description:
`complete` | `per-path` — what ONE capture restates (default `complete`).
A SEPARATE AXIS from `temporalSemantics`: `complete` means every capture
restates the whole population (a coverage report, a test run), so the
temporal fold applies directly. `per-path` means a capture restates only the
paths in its snapshot — which is what a **tree collector over a per-commit delta**
does. Such a measure is folded to the latest capture per (producer, path)
before aggregating, so a repo-wide total stays correct while only changed
files are rescanned. Set this on any measure a snapshot-triggered collector
emits per-file facts on.

MetricEntry.description:
One entry in the top-level `metrics:` block — a **pure read-time SPEC** over a
measure. A metric no longer *computes* anything: it names a
`sourceMeasure` + an `aggregation` (+ optional `filter`), or a `formula` over
other metrics, and the engine aggregates the durable facts a `collectors:` entry
emitted. Two forms, distinguished by which key is set:
- **`use:`** — enable an existing catalog metric by key (built-in/global),
  optionally overriding `target`/thresholds for this project.
- **`key:`** — define a NEW spec (`sourceMeasure` + `aggregation`, or `formula`).

Resolved across the three scopes into [`ResolvedSpec`]s. All non-discriminant
fields are optional so both forms share one struct; validation enforces the
per-form rules.

use.description: `use:` form — the catalog key to enable.

key.description: `key:` form — the new metric's namespaced key.

enabled.description:
Active flag. `None`/`Some(true)` = active (a bare `use:`/`key:` entry is
on); `Some(false)` = an explicit **disable marker** kept in config so a
default-ON metric (producer/extension) or a config-defined metric can be
turned off without deleting its definition. Not a structural field, so a
`use:` entry may carry it (unlike measure/aggregation/filter/formula).

default.description:
An extension metric's default: `on` (the default) is active unless
the project turns it off (`enabled: false`); `off` is active only
while the project lists it with `use:`.

collector.description:
An extension metric's collector: the id of the collector in the same
extension that computes its facts. A collector some metric names
runs only while one of those metrics is active.

sourceMeasure.description:
The measure whose facts this metric aggregates (required for a `key:`
metric unless it sets `formula`). NULL for a pure formula metric.

aggregation.description:
`count` | `sum` | `avg` | `min` | `max` | `last` | `ratio` (default `last`).
Combines the facts WITHIN a capture; cross-time collapse is governed by the
source measure's `temporalSemantics`.

formula.description:
Derived-metric formula over other metric keys (mutually exclusive with
`sourceMeasure`).

language.description: Language this metric measures (e.g. `rust`), for the catalog filter.

description.description:
One-line human description (shown atop the Metric Detail page). Inherent to
the definition — a `use:` can't override.

sliceableDims.description: Conformed-dimension keys this metric can be sliced by (drill-across).

entity.description:
Entity metric: the `v_*` view it aggregates, instead of a
measure's facts. Fragments below are SQL over that view, aliased `e`.

where.description: Entity metric: which rows count (a SQL condition).

time.description:
Entity metric: the timestamp column/expression that makes it an EVENT
metric (rows bucketed by when they happened). Without it the metric is
a STATE metric: its current value, captured over time.

value.description: Entity metric: the value expression aggregated (not needed for `count`).

MetricDefault.description:
Whether an extension's metric is active before the project says
anything about it ([`MetricEntry::default`]).

FilterConfig.description:
A fact predicate on a `metrics:` spec (the `filter:` block) — the config
mirror of the engine's `FactFilter`. A conjunctive predicate
keeping only the facts that match before aggregation: `minValue` for a
count-over-threshold (complexity ≥ N), `severity` for a lint slice, `dimEq`
for a conformed-dimension slice (`[oxplow.rule, unsafe_block]`).

maxValue.description: Keep facts with `value <= maxValue` (`0`: the untested files).

severity.description: Keep facts whose reported severity equals this (e.g. `error`).

dimEq.description: Keep facts whose dimension `[key]` equals `[value]` — a 2-element list.

FormulaConfig.description:
A derived-metric formula on a `metrics:` spec (the `formula:` block) — a
constrained binary op over two OTHER metric keys (no source measure). The
engine aligns the two metrics on their shared rollup key and applies `op`
(`div` is the ratio primitive: bugs-per-KLOC, cost-per-token).

DimensionEntry.description:
One entry in the top-level `dimensions:` block — the **conformed-dimension
catalog** authoring surface. A dimension is a
slice axis that means the same thing to every fact that carries it
(`oxplow.severity`, `acme.license`, …), enabling cross-metric drill-across.
Like [`MeasureEntry`] it is definition-only; the `oxplow.*` built-ins are the
migration seed. Resolved by [`resolve_dimensions`] and seeded into the
`dimension` table at boot; `promote` requests a generated column + index
(catalog teeth).

key.description: The new dimension's namespaced key (`<vendor>.<id>`). Required.

subjectKind.description: For `entity-ref` dims — the subject kind the value points at.

vocabulary.description: Optional controlled vocabulary (the allowed value set).

promote.description:
Request a generated column + expression index on `fact` for this dim
(fast group-by/filter). Off by default — the long tail lives in
`dims_json`, promoted only when hot.

entity.description:
Entity dimension: the `v_*` view it slices, for entity
metrics over the same view.

expr.description: Entity dimension: the SQL expression (over the view, aliased `e`).

join.description:
Entity dimension: an optional join, e.g.
`LEFT JOIN v_thread t ON t.id = e.thread_id`.

RawCollector.description:
A `collectors:` entry as written (an extension's manifest, or
`.oxplow/project.yaml`); `validate` makes it a `CollectorSpec`.

id.description: Unique in its owner; a dotted id (`repo.scan_clone`) is fine.

entry.description:
The program or script, relative to its owner's folder; a report
collector's `oxplow:<parser>`.

provider.description: For `read`: the provider collector it runs.

trigger.description: When it runs by itself; absent, `manual`.

sync.description: How a run's entities land; absent, `replace`.

needs.description:
The services its script uses beyond what its kind implies (a
Starlark collector's).

whole_tree.description: A fact collector that reads the whole tree on every run.

RuntimeName.description:
The names `runtime:` takes. Its schema only: `validate` reads the
text, to say what's wrong in its own words.

ProviderRead.description: A provider's collector a `read` collector runs.

instance.description:
The instance, `<extension>/<instance id>` (a provider's default
instance has the provider's id).

TriggerFile.description: `trigger:` as written: `manual`, or a map of a trigger's keys.

TriggerMap.description:
A trigger's keys. Which go together `parse_trigger` checks, and says
in its own words.

on.description: The event types it runs on.

where.description: With `on`: payload fields and the values they must equal.

on_run.description: A report collector's: after a `test` or `analysis` run.

settle.description: With `on`: run once no triggering event has arrived for this long.

at_most.description: With `on`: run at most this often.

idle.description: With `on`: run once nothing has happened for this long.

force.description: With `on` and a pacing key: event types that run at once.

EventTypeList.description: One event type, or a list of them.

RunKind.description: The kind of run a report collector reads after.

RawInput.description: `input` as written: its SQL, or `{ sql, limit }`.

oneOf.description: Each run restates every entity (one it doesn't mention is emptied).

Each run adds or updates rows by key, and removes the keys it lists
under `deleted`; an entity it doesn't mention is left alone.

ColumnShape.description:
An entity column as written: its type, or `{ type, doc }`. Its schema
only: `validate` reads the two, to say what's wrong in its own words.

ColumnType.description: Declared type of an entity column.

oneOf.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp, stored as text.

EntityRelation.description:
A documented join from an entity to another view. Not executed; it
tells agents and lens authors how the data connects.

to.description: The view it joins to, e.g. `v_work_item` or `v_github_review`.

on.description: The SQL join condition, e.g. `v_github_pr.head_branch = v_stream.branch`.

Records.description:
What a report collector records: its parser's typed output, merged
into the run (`.context/collection.md`).

oneOf.description: A suite/case tree of test outcomes (a `test-run`).
Per-file instrumented/covered lines (a coverage capture).
Linter/analyzer findings (a `static-analysis` capture).

CommandFile.description: A `commands:` entry as the manifest holds it.

job.description: A durable job's model may call it.

lifecycle.description: `experimental` keeps a bundled extension's command experimental.

example.description:
An input that fits its schema: what an agent is shown beside the
schema and a refused input quotes. A script's defaults to its
first example that runs.

tool.description:
Offer it to agents as an MCP tool too, named
`<namespace>_<tool>` ([`tool_name`]).

unrecorded.description:
Its input's properties kept out of its record (a token, a key), or
`*` for all of it.

CommandUi.description:
A command as a person meets it (`.context/commands.md` "Offering a
command to a person"). Agents ignore it.

label.description: What a person reads: `Pull Changes`, `New Task…`.

keywords.description: More words search matches it by.

about.description:
The ref kind it acts on (`work_item`, `effort`): offered on that
ref's page and rows. `None`: it needs no ref, and search offers it.

form.description:
What gathers its input — a page (a tab id, `oxplow:oxplow/page?page=new-task`) or one
of the window's own forms (`new-thread`, `commit`): choosing it
opens that rather than running it.

open_after.description:
The page to open once it ran: a tab id whose `{{result.<field>}}`
takes the result's field (`oxplow:oxplow/dashboard?id={{result.id}}`).

background.description:
It runs as a background task (a slow call out: pull, push) whose
failure is reported, rather than awaited where it was chosen.

shortcut.description:
The key that runs it, as `Ctrl/Cmd+S` / `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+N`
(`Ctrl/Cmd` is Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere).

while_typing.description:
Its shortcut runs it while the person types in a field too (Save,
Find); otherwise typing keeps it.

menu.description: Where the menu bar shows it.

when.description:
When it's offered — in search, the menu bar and by its shortcut —
in VS Code's when-clause syntax over the window's context keys
(`crate::when`): `fileShown && fileDirty`, `streamKind == worktree`.
Absent, always.

MenuPlace.description:
A command's place in the menu bar: which menu, the group it sits in
(VS Code's: groups are sorted by name and drawn apart by a separator)
and where in the group (lowest first).

group.description: Its group (`1_project`, `2_save`); absent, the menu's first.

JobFile.description: The on-disk shape, with unknown fields refused by serde.

tools.description:
This extension's commands (their names as declared, without the
namespace) the model may call; each says `job: true`.

max_tool_rounds.description:
Model rounds at most (1–16, default 4): a round that calls tools
is followed by another with their results.

timeout.description: Seconds it may run (1–600, default 120) before it fails.

oneOf.description:
An attempt cut off (a restart, a lost lease) ends the job
`interrupted`.

The job can run again from its first request: an attempt cut off
is queued again, up to `MAX_ATTEMPTS` in all, and its
`contribution.job.completed` is logged once, at its final end.

AiProfileFile.description: The on-disk shape, with unknown fields refused by serde.

description.description: What the profile is for (at most 4096 bytes).

fallback.description: The built-in role whose model serves it until a model is bound.

features.description: What the bound model must support.

FallbackFile.description: The built-in roles a profile may fall back to.

FeatureFile.description: What a bound model must support.

PageFile.description: A `pages:` entry as the manifest holds it.

label.description:
What its tab says, when not its `title`: `{{param.<name>}}` filled
from what it shows (a renderer's URI, a route's `params`).

category.description:
Its launcher section; leave it out for a page only opened from
elsewhere.

params.description:
The params naming what it shows, in its URI's `?`; its lens's filters
and selections ride in the `#` view.

count.description: A `number` lens of this extension whose value is the launcher badge.

lens.description: A lens of this extension that draws the page …

component.description: … or `oxplow:<name>`, a built-in (oxplow's own extension only).

for.description:
The resources it renders — one or a list: `oxplow/file`, its own
`<extension>/<name>`, another extension's, or `https` / `http` (a
web page). A URI of one opens on it; without `for` it is a route.

accepts.description:
Which URIs of those it takes, by param: `present`, `absent`, or an
anchored pattern (`^git:`) the value matches.

default.description:
What its resource opens on when the URI's view names no renderer:
only for a resource this extension declares, one per resource.

pinned.description: Its tab leads the strip and isn't evicted (a renderer only).

comments.description: Its text takes comments, anchored to its URI.

LauncherCategory.description:
Launcher (Cmd+K) sections a lens can be listed under. Mirrors the
renderer's `PageCategory`.

Renders.description: A page's `for`: one resource or several.

PanelFile.description: A `panels:` entry as the manifest holds it.

PanelScope.description:
What a left-nav panel is bound to: the project, the current stream, or
the current thread — which of `stream_id` / `thread_id` its lenses get.

UiBlock.description:
`ui:` — everything an extension adds to the core UI: lenses mounted
into core pages (`slots`), decorations on core refs (`decorators`) and
replaced sub-components (`replacements`). Its commands
meet a person through their own `ui` (`commands:`).

slots.description:
Lenses mounted into core pages: `{ slot, lens }`, typed one by one
([`slots_of`]).

decorators.description: Labels from its models on core refs.

replacements.description: A lens in place of a named core component.

SlotMount.description:
A slot mount: a lens into a core page, or among a document or
dashboard lens's parts.

at.description:
Where among the page's parts (a parts slot only): `start`, `end`,
`{ after: <id> }`, `{ before: <id> }`. Default `end`.

title.description: Its heading in the page; else the lens's title.

SlotAt.description:
Where a mount goes among a page's parts: `start`, `end` (the default),
or `{ after: <id> }` / `{ before: <id> }` beside one of them. An id the
page no longer has means the end (and a load warning), so a page that
changes never loses what an extension adds.

SlotEdge.description: The ends of a page's parts.

TileSize.description:
How much of a dashboard a tile takes: one cell, two across, two down,
or the whole row.

DecoratorFile.description: A `ui.decorators` entry as the manifest holds it.

oneOf.description: A chip in the header of a page whose ref the model lists.
A badge after a lens cell that links to a listed ref.

ReplacementFile.description: A `ui.replacements` entry as the manifest holds it.

version.description:
The props contract's version it was written against; checked
against the table's, so a changed contract refuses it rather than
handing it props it doesn't know.

oneOf.description:
After each agent tool call; results go to the agent as that call's
context and are recorded as nudges.
On each prompt the human sends; results join the prompt's context.

When a turn ends (its `thread.checkpoint`): what the turn left
behind, delivered when the agent next hears from oxplow (the next
prompt, else the next tool call).

AdvisoryOncePer.description: How often the same advisory may reach the agent.

oneOf.description: Once per effort, the first time the query returns rows.

Once per thread per `key` value: each row's `key` column fires
once (put `:effort_id` in the key for once per effort per row).
Every time, whenever the query returns rows.
Once per thread, the first time the query returns rows.
Once per agent session on the thread (the harness's session id).
Once per thread per day (UTC).
The coding agent: delivered on its next prompt or tool call.
A person: raised in Alerts until they dismiss it.

EventTypesFile.description:
`event_types:` as the manifest holds it; each type is read on its own
(one that doesn't parse is its error, not the block's).

schema.description: A JSON file in the folder.

ResourceEntry.description:
A `resources:` entry as a manifest holds it. `resolve` and `searchable`
name models as the manifest does; the app's loader turns them into the
views they publish as and checks them (`extension_resources`).

title.description: The column of `resolve` that titles one (default `title`).

ParamDecl.description:
One of a resource's params: whether every URI carries it, and the
pattern its (decoded) value matches, anchored by its author.

WikilinkDecl.description:
`[[<prefix>:<value>]]` sugar: a wikilink with this prefix names the
resource with `param` set to the value (`[[git:abc1234]]` → a commit).

ImplementationFile.description: An `implementations:` entry as the manifest holds it.

config.description: What it configures, checked against the built-in's schema.

needs.description:
The scopes a policy script calls (`sql.read`): only what a script
can (`scope_calls::CALLABLE`).

icon.description:
A path to an SVG in the extension (`icons/claude.svg`): its logo,
shown wherever the implementation is (a session's tab). Any
capability may declare one.

SkillFile.description: A `skills:` entry as the manifest holds it.

SkillKind.description: What the agent's runtime makes of it.

oneOf.description: A skill the agent loads when it's relevant: `<name>/SKILL.md`.
A slash command the person runs: `/oxplow:<name>`.

id.description:
The provider's id: its program's approval (`<extension>/<id>`) and
the id of its default instance — an instance's id is its refs'
segment (`oxplow:oxplow/work_item?id=…&provider=<id>`) and its commands' namespace
(`<id>.estimate`).

entry.description: The program, relative to the extension folder — or `adapter`.

adapter.description: An MCP server run through oxplow's adapter, instead of an `entry`.

env.description: Host environment variables passed through by name.

credentials.description:
Credentials it gets from the keychain, as environment variables:
each a name (a value the person pastes) or `{ name, oauth }` (one
they sign in for; the variable holds the access token).

network.description: Hosts it may reach (enforced where the OS can).

declarations.description: The checked-in `InitializeResult` (JSON), relative to the folder.

idPattern.description:
What a work list's own ids look like (a regex matched whole:
`[A-Z]+-\d+`), so a loose id resolves to its item while it's the
active work list.

fields.description:
A work list's own fields (kept in an item's `native`), so screens
render and edit them: `[{ name, title, kind: enum|text|number,
values? }]`.

needs.description:
The scopes it calls over the protocol (`host/call`,
`sql.read` or `state.read`): part of what its approval covers, and the only ones it
may call.

AdapterSpec.description:
An MCP server as a provider: oxplow's adapter runs `mcp`'s
server and translates through `mapping`, refusing a server whose tools
aren't `tools`.

mapping.description: The Starlark mapping (`transform(x)`), relative to the folder.

tools.description: The pinned tools (`[{ name, description, inputSchema }]`, JSON).

McpServer.description: How the adapter reaches the MCP server: exactly one of the two.

anyOf.description: A program in the folder, spoken to over its stdio.

A server reached over streamable HTTP. `auth` names the
credential whose value is sent as its bearer token.

CredentialDecl.description: A credential's name (a value the person pastes), or `{ name, oauth }` (one they sign in for).

CredentialFile.description: A credential written out: `{ name, oauth? }`.

name.description: The environment variable the provider reads it from.

oauth.description: Obtained by signing in rather than pasted.

OAuthDecl.description:
How a credential is obtained by signing in: OAuth 2.1's
authorization-code flow with PKCE, run by oxplow — the provider only
ever sees the access token.

token_url.description: Where a code, or a refresh token, is exchanged for an access token.

client_secret.description:
The **name** of another (static) credential of this provider that
holds the client secret, for a service that requires one.

redirect_port.description:
The loopback port the redirect comes back on, for a service that
wants one registered; any free port otherwise.

client_auth.description:
How the client secret is sent with a token request: `basic` (an
`Authorization` header, RFC 6749 §2.3.1 — what every service must
take; the default) or `post` (in the form, for a service that wants
that).

ClientAuth.description: How a client authenticates to a token endpoint.

SecretRef.description:
A versioned reference. Only the host can create a fresh identity; a wire
reference conveys identity alone and must be resolved under host authority.

FieldDecl.description:
One of a work list's own fields: kept in an item's `native` under
`name`, declared so screens render and edit it without knowing which
list is active.

values.description:
An `enum`'s values, in the order they're offered (empty for any
other kind).

read_only.description:
Set by the list itself (who filed it, when it synced): shown, never
edited — a `oxplow.work_item.update` that names it is refused.

FieldKind.description: What kind of value a declared field holds.

oneOf.description: One of `values`.

EffectFile.description:
An `effects:` entry as the manifest holds it; `on` and `where` are read
by the collectors' trigger rules (`parse_trigger`).

on.description: The event types it reacts to.

where.description: Payload fields and the values they must equal.

ComponentFile.description: A `custom_components:` entry as the manifest holds it.

sql.description:
`read`: it runs its own read-only SQL over the models
(`querySql`); its extension needs `permissions.sql: read`.
